headline: Blue Jays outlast Phillies in 11 innings, 7-5
recap: The Phillies fell to the Toronto Blue Jays 7-5 in 11 innings on Saturday at Citizens Bank Park, their second straight loss. Toronto took a 2-0 lead through three innings before Philadelphia scored four runs in the sixth to go up 4-2; Trea Turner and Bryce Harper each hit solo home runs, and Justin Crawford (triple) and Brandon Marsh (sacrifice fly) also drove in runs. Jose Alvarado blew the save with a two-run eighth that tied it at 4-4, and the score was still 5-5 through ten before Toronto scored twice in the 11th to win it. Aaron Nola started and allowed two runs over five innings for Philadelphia. Chase Shugart (2-1) took the loss, Louis Varland got the win, and Lazaro Estrada earned the save for Toronto.
The loss dropped Philadelphia to 62-56, second in the NL East, 8.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (70-47), and extended the team's losing streak to two.

The Phillies close out the series against Toronto today, Sunday, first pitch 1:35 PM ET at Citizens Bank Park. Jesus Luzardo starts for Philadelphia against Blue Jays right-hander Shane Bieber. DraftKings has the Phillies as -203 moneyline favorites.
